plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms stand on sturdy stems in bold rows across the Dutch bulb fields. They turn the countryside into ribbons of saturated color. Tulips are at or near their peak in the last third of April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to early May in the Netherlands, with peak color in late April
plants.location: Lisse and the Bollenstreek bulb region, Netherlands
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs were so prized in the Netherlands that single bulbs reportedly sold for more than a skilled craftsman earned in a year.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: Bare branches and even trunks are covered in clusters of magenta-pink, pea-like flowers before the heart-shaped leaves unfold. It is a classic sign of spring in woodlands and gardens. In much of the eastern United States, bloom runs through April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to late April, depending on latitude
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, including the Appalachian foothills and mid-Atlantic woodlands
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a slightly tangy taste. The tree is in the pea family, and its flowers can grow straight from the trunk, a trait called cauliflory.

plants.name: Prunus serrulata
plants.description: Bright pink blossoms fill the branches in delicate clusters. In cooler northern Japan, the season arrives later than in Tokyo or Kyoto. Parks there fill with picnickers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to early May in Hokkaido and northern Tohoku, after earlier blooms farther south
plants.funFact: The Japanese tradition of hanami, or flower viewing, dates back more than a thousand years. Forecasters now track the cherry blossom front as it moves north across the country.
